title: Senior Product Manager (w/m/d)
description: <div class="content-intro"><p><strong>Who We Are </strong></p> <p>Verve has created a more efficient and privacy-focused way to buy and monetize advertising. Verve is an ecosystem of demand and supply technologies fusing data, media, and technology together to deliver results and growth to both advertisers and publishers–no matter the screen or location, no matter who, what, or where a customer is. With offices across the globe and with an eye on servicing forward-thinking advertising customers, Verve’s solutions are trusted by more than 90 of the United States’ top 100 advertisers, 4,000 publishers globally, and the world’s top demand-side platforms. Learn more at <a href="https://verve.com/">verve.com</a>.<strong><br></strong></p></div><p><strong>Who You Are</strong></p> <p>We are currently seeking a Senior Product Manager to own our Identity Graph / Enrichment & Audience Enhancement products. title: Staff Platform Engineer, Fanatics Markets - UK
description: <div class="content-intro"><h2 class="job-details__description-header text-color-secondary font-family-secondary" data-bind="i18n: 'job-details.employer-description-title'">About Us</h2> <div class="job-details__description-content basic-formatter" data-bind="html: pageData().job.corporateDescription"> <p>Fanatics is a leading global sports platform redefining how fans connect with the teams, players and moments they love. Our businesses — Fanatics Commerce, Fanatics Collectibles, Fanatics Betting & Gaming, Fanatics Events, Fanatics Advertising, Fanatics Markets and Fanatics Studios — maximize the presence and reach for hundreds of partners globally and create a one-stop experience that allows fans to buy, bet, collect, and earn, while engaging with sports in deeper, more immersive ways. This includes licensed fan gear and lifestyle products, sportsbook and iGaming, physical and digital trading cards, live events, premium sports entertainment content, credit card offerings and more. Together, they form a powerful, integrated ecosystem — connected by the Fanatics ONE loyalty program and FanCash, the currency of sport — delivering personalized experiences to over 100 million fans worldwide. Fanatics holds partnerships with over 900 sports properties, from professional leagues and players’ associations to teams, colleges and retail partners; over 7,000 athletes and celebrities; and over 2,000 retail locations, including all Lids stores. Backed by a team of more than 22,000 employees, Fanatics is committed to relentlessly enhancing the fan experience.</p> </div> <p> </p></div><h2><strong>About the Team</strong></h2> <p>Fanatics Markets is the real-money prediction and trading app where you can invest in moments you care about. Built on a secure platform, we let users predict real-world outcomes and trade on events they actually follow—from sports and entertainment to political elections and beyond. Our mission is to redefine how fans engage with the moments and markets that matter most. We're looking for the right people to help us build the future of prediction markets.</p> <p><strong>Role Overview</strong></p> <p>As a Staff Software Engineer within our Platform team, you will help define the technical direction of the platform underpinning our exchange and trading systems. You will lead the design and evolution of our infrastructure and platform standards to support a highly available, low-latency exchange, partnering closely with exchange engineers and engineering leads to enable rapid innovation without compromising stability or security.</p> <p>This role requires a balance of deep hands-on software engineering, systems thinking and technical leadership. You will lead complex projects that support the exchange—from load-testing environments and mock integrations to monitoring and automated recovery. You will turn ambiguous requirements into practical designs, own delivery from ideation to production and help operate the platform as the exchange goes live. The balance of coding and infrastructure work varies by project, but you should be comfortable independently developing new software as well as improving existing systems, setting platform standards and mentoring engineers across experience levels.</p> <p>On the engineering side, we are pioneering the use of AI as a code collaborator. We need engineers who have moved beyond experimentation—who actively use tools like Claude Code, Cursor, or GitHub Copilot to ship production code faster while maintaining exceptional quality.</p> <h2><strong>Responsibilities</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Lead the design and development of software tools, services and automation that solve complex infrastructure, reliability and developer experience challenges.</li> <li>Define and evolve the architecture of highly available cloud-native infrastructure, balancing performance, reliability, security and cost as the platform grows.</li> <li>Set technical direction for CI/CD pipelines and developer tooling, remaining hands-on in delivering improvements to the software delivery lifecycle.</li> <li>Lead the development of load-testing environments and supporting software, including mock services and integrations.</li> <li>Establish and evolve standards for AI-augmented development, using effective prompting and validation practices to increase velocity without sacrificing code quality.</li> <li>Identify and mitigate AI-generated code pitfalls, such as security vulnerabilities or over-abstraction, and help teams evaluate the impact on quality and productivity.</li> <li>Guide the design and implementation of platform security safeguards and compliance standards to protect the integrity of the firm’s systems.</li> <li>Shape the system observability roadmap and lead improvements to monitoring, tracing, alerting and automated recovery.</li> <li>Partner with exchange, product and engineering leads to resolve architectural trade-offs, align priorities and deliver scalable platform solutions.</li> <li>Mentor engineers across experience levels, lead technical design discussions and raise engineering standards across teams.</li> <li>Participate in the on-call rotation, lead incident response for team-owned services and drive engineering improvements that prevent recurring incidents.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>Skills</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Significant experience in software, backend or platform engineering, with a track record of leading complex technical projects and delivering production software and scalable, cloud-native environments.</li> <li>Deep software development expertise, including the ability to independently design, build, test and deploy services or substantial tools from scratch and guide others through complex implementation decisions.</li> <li>Deep hands-on Kubernetes experience, including designing and operating production environments, troubleshooting complex failures, and establishing patterns for high availability and efficient scaling.</li> <li>Strong hands-on experience with AWS and infrastructure as code using Terraform, including making architectural decisions across complex environments.</li> <li>High proficiency in Java and Python; Go is a plus. You should be comfortable bridging the gap between infrastructure and application logic.</li> <li>Deep understanding of distributed systems and the ability to make and explain trade-offs between low latency, high availability, scalability and operational complexity.</li> <li>Experience shaping CI/CD and observability approaches, with hands-on knowledge of tools such as Prometheus, Grafana or Datadog.</li> <li>Strong proficiency in using AI collaborators such as Claude Code, Cursor or GitHub Copilot to ship production code and improve engineering workflows.</li> <li>Ability to evaluate AI-generated code for security gaps or architectural errors and establish rigorous testing and validation practices.</li> <li>Proven ability to turn ambiguous problems into a clear technical direction and deliver improvements across team boundaries, balancing immediate needs with long-term architectural health.</li> <li>Strong communication skills, including the ability to explain complex technical decisions, influence without formal authority and collaborate effectively with distributed engineering and product teams.</li> <li>Experience mentoring senior engineers and building alignment around technical standards and architectural decisions.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>Preferred Qualifications</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Experience in high-growth startup environments.</li> <li>Experience with financial systems, exchanges, real-money transactions or regulatory compliance.</li> <li>Background in designing and building internal developer platforms, tools, CLI applications or infrastructure automation services.</li> <li>Experience developing load-testing environments, mock services or automated recovery systems.</li> <li>Experience leading technical initiatives spanning multiple teams or evolving platform architecture through significant growth or change.</li> </ul> <p>Depending on the role, your interview and onboarding experience may include in-person components, such as onsite interviews or Launching into Better: LIVE—a multi-day cultural immersion in New York City for full-time, non-seasonal hires. These sessions are designed to build connection and bring our culture to life, though specific travel and participation requirements will be confirmed based on your role and location. Your recruiter will provide clear guidance at each stage of the process.</p> <p>Ready to build the future of sports betting? If you possess some of these skills but not all of them, we still encourage you to apply! Please note that <strong>visa sponsorship is not available</strong> for this position. We are open to <strong>fully remote candidates based in the United Kingdom.</strong> Remote employees may also be eligible for a home office setup stipend.</p> <p>#LI-Remote</p> <p>#LI-AL1 </p><div class="content-conclusion"><p></p> <p>By submitting your application, you agree to our terms of service and acknowledge you have read our <a href="https://static1.squarespace.com/static/5ff494b9931735466ce28d5b/t/69de53bde2c02c25e9c38758/1776178110037/Candidate+Privacy+Policy+April+2026.pdf" target="_blank">Candidate Privacy Policy.</a></p> <p><em>Fanatics will never ask candidates for money, banking information, or other sensitive personal information as part of the interview process. If you receive a suspicious message claiming to be from Fanatics recruiting, please do not respond and report it </em><a ----- <p></p></div> Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Product Manager
description: <div> <p><strong>Weekly office requirement:</strong> Monday/Wednesday weekly <br><strong>Employment type:</strong> Permanent<br><strong>Seniority level: </strong>Mid-senior</p> <p>At GWI we’re always looking for extraordinary people who thrive on making an extraordinary impact. Right now we’re looking for a<strong> Product Manager </strong>to play a key role in our <strong>User Management (Revenue </strong><strong>& Enablement) </strong>team in <strong>London</strong>. If that’s you, and making a difference gets you out of bed in the morning, keep reading. It could be the start of something, well, extraordinary.</p> <br> <h1>Sounds great, what will I be doing? 🤔</h1> <p>As our Product Manager you'll own the systems that make GWI's subscription and consumption business run, such as billing, metering, user plans, feature access, product analytics and user messaging. It's the layer everything else sits on. Get it right and GWI can price, package and sell in new ways.</p> <br> <p>Two big pieces of work sit at the heart of this role. The first is billing for our consumption products, which is an area we're actively developing, and one you'll help shape. The second is making our internal tools talk to each other properly, so user data flows consistently between them and Salesforce, and everyone across the business is working from the same picture. Most of your stakeholders are internal - Revenue Operations, Finance, Business Intelligence, Client Success and Engineering - with some direct client contact along the way. You'll lead one squad of front-end and back-end engineers and a designer, alongside the PM and Engineers in our sister squad, Identity & Access - together you cover the whole of User Management.</p> <br> <p>A few things you’ll be responsible for: </p> <br>👉 Connecting our internal user management tools with Salesforce and each other, so data flows consistently and user information is mapped the same way everywhere <p>👉 Billing for our consumption products - metering, API usage, payment flows and user plans</p> <p>👉 Customer feature flags, access and management - who can see what, and why</p> <p>👉 Product analytics - event firing, sign-up flow data, usage data - so the business can see what's happening and act on it</p> <p>👉 Building the roadmap from client feedback, internal stakeholder input and usage analytics, and prioritising the most valuable work</p> <p>👉 Scoping the work and owning how your squad delivers it<br><br>It’s also fun; shaking things up is what working for GWI is all about. You’ll need to be flexible, comfortable with continuous change, and working in a high-tempo environment.</p> <br> <h1>What do I need to bring with me? 🧳</h1> <p>You’ll need to be able to demonstrate the core skills this role requires. You don't have to tick all the boxes right away; the important thing is that you’re willing to learn. Here’s what the team will be looking for in you:</p> <br> <p>👉 You've shipped products at a B2B company</p> <p>👉 You've built complex roadmaps with cross-functional dependencies, and you can balance multiple priorities without losing the plot</p> <p>👉 You make informed decisions at pace, even when the picture isn't complete</p> <p>👉 You're a strong problem solver, negotiator and influencer — you get alignment without needing authority</p> <p>👉 You explain complex things clearly to very different audiences: execs, engineers, customers</p> <p>👉 You ask questions and draw knowledge out of your team to find the right engineering and design solutions</p> <p>👉 You make informed decisions at pace, even when the picture isn't complete, and you're happy taking a big initiative and running with it</p> <p>👉 Bonus points if you've worked with Salesforce before, or with tools that need to sync data between systems and internal user management systems.</p> <p><br>Equally important is attitude. We want people who think big (to make an impact), ask why (to find a better way), and show respect (to everyone, at every level, all the time). Those are our values, and they’re a big part of what we’re looking for in you.</p> <br> <h1>Why Join Us</h1> <p>👉 You'll work on how GWI packages its consumption products - commercial problems with real weight behind them</p> <p>👉 Your squad owns infrastructure the whole company depends on, so the work gets noticed</p> <p>👉 You'll build relationships across the business, from Finance to Engineering to the Exec team</p> <p>👉 You'll learn from a senior PM who knows this space, with room to run your own squad your way</p> </div> <p> </p> <h1>Diversity, Equity & Inclusion 🫶</h1> <p>Diversity is fundamental to who we are—as a data company and as a workplace. title: Principal Compliance Officer
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today, SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of making life multiplanetary and expanding consciousness to the stars.<br><br>SpaceXSI is building Super Intelligence to help humanity understand the universe. Our teams are building the full Super Intelligence stack: from our Colossus supercomputers, to Grok models, to our suite of applications, including Grok Bot, Grok Build, Grok Imagine, Grok Voice, and X. We're creating a powerful flywheel where more compute trains better models, better models power more useful products, and what we learn from people using those products shapes what we build next.</p></div><h4><strong>PRINCIPAL COMPLIANCE OFFICER</strong></h4> <p>The UK financial crime program is being built now, and it has to stand up to the FCA. This role sits in Compliance, reports to the US BSA/AML Officer, and owns the UK framework end to end — AML/CTF, sanctions, fraud, ABC, KYC/CDD/EDD, transaction monitoring, SARs, and the operating rhythm. You will still work the hard cases. It is a builder seat with accountability, not a queue job with “strategy” in the title.</p> <p>If you have eight or more years inside an FCA-regulated bank, EMI, PI, or payments firm, have owned or rebuilt a financial crime control framework, and can still open a file, this is the seat. You will build the UK program from the ground up, setting the standards the team and the FCA will use. This is consumer-scale payments financial crime work – not a private-banking book – and you’ll sit directly with Product and Engineering. You’ll operate in a small team with a direct line to the US BSA/AML Officer, where scope is broad and process is lean. The measure of success is a program that still works a year later, and the role sits alongside MLRO / SMF17-adjacent duties for the UK entity.</p> <h4><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></h4> <ul> <li>Design and run the UK financial crime programme: policy, procedures, CDD/EDD, risk rating, sanctions screening, transaction monitoring, SAR handling, escalation, QA, and training</li> <li>Turn MLR 2017, POCA, the Sanctions and Anti-Money Laundering Act, JMLSG, the FCA Financial Crime Guide, SYSC 6.3, and payments/EMI expectations into something operations and product can run</li> <li>Own the UK business-wide risk assessment and keep it honest as the product, customer mix, and channels change</li> <li>Handle complex cases — PEPs, adverse media, sanctions hits, high-risk onboarding, fraud typologies, escalations — then use the queue to fix the framework</li> <li>Stand up first- and second-line controls: documentation, workflows, vendor oversight, quality sampling, MI, and issue management</li> <li>Put UK requirements into the customer journey with Legal, Operations, Product, and Engineering. Be the UK voice in global design decisions</li> <li>Report on quality, residual risk, throughput, and control health, and prepare the program for internal audit, skilled-person reviews, and FCA scrutiny</li> <li>Build the operating model as the team grows.</li> <li>Hire, coach, and set the standard</li> <li>Support MLRO / SMF17-adjacent duties as the UK permissions model requires</li> </ul> <h4><strong>BASiC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></h4> <ul> <li>8+ years of hands-on experience with financial crime in a regulated UK firm (bank, EMI, PI, payments, or e-money), including substantial KYC/CDD/EDD</li> </ul> <h4><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></h4> <ul> <li>You will still do the cases, close gaps in a small team, do not wait for a 30-page RACI</li> <li>You know the UK regime well enough to argue a point — MLR 2017, JMLSG, POCA, UK sanctions, FCA expectations — and how it lands in a payments product</li> <li>You have designed or rebuilt a framework, procedure, or control, not only cleared files or written a policy nobody ran</li> <li>You have led people or a workstream. You can defend a risk decision and explain it to the Product without jargon</li> <li>EU financial crime experience</li> <li>Experience with the EU AML package, 6AMLD, EBA guidelines, national transposition, or an EU FIU/regulator, especially on cross-border payments, wallets, or EMI/PI products (useful because X Money will not stay inside one perimeter)</li> </ul> <h4><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></h4> <ul> <li>In-office five days a week; occasional work-from-home when needed</li> </ul> <h4><strong>COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:</strong></h4> <ul> <li>Competitive base + equity</li> <li>UK private medical covering GPs and specialists; pension; life insurance</li> <li>25 days’ paid time off; lunch and dinner allowance</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><em>SpaceXSI is an equal opportunity employer. For details on data processing, view our </em><em><a href="https://x.ai/legal/recruitment-privacy-notice" target="_blank">Recruitment Privacy Notice</a>.</em></p></div> Find Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: VP of Engineering
description: We built ClearBank on the belief that banking infrastructure would no longer slow down progress. Instead, it would be a catalyst that unlocks the potential to innovate. It would adapt to different needs so a new era in financial services could begin. We’re here to challenge the status quo in banking, are you? We all know that transforming banking forever is not an easy mission, but we’re more than ready to rise to that challenge. We all do it every day; navigating new, unexpected and sometimes even daunting challenges. But we believe in ourselves and trust we can do it. Want to innovate? Go for it. Push for a better way? You Can. If you think you have it in you, this is Where You Can. About Us ClearBank is a technology‑enabled, fully regulated bank providing cloud‑based banking and payments infrastructure to financial institutions. We operate at scale in a highly regulated environment, where trust, resilience and security are critical. Our engineering organisation is focused on enabling frequent, reliable change while maintaining strong controls. We believe quality is not a gate at the end of delivery, but something designed in from the very start. Role Purpose This is a senior leadership role accountable for the strategy, design, build, operation and ongoing resilience of ClearBank’s payments and cards platforms. The VP of Payments & Cards will lead multiple engineering teams responsible for real-time, scheme-connected payments and cards systems across the UK, Europe, and future international markets. This requires deep experience working close to the infrastructure that moves money. Ideally, this will include direct integration with major payment schemes or rails, such as FPS, Bacs or CHAPS in the UK, SEPA payment schemes in Europe, or ACH and Fedwire in the US. We will also consider experience gained through payment infrastructure providers or connectivity platforms provided it includes sufficient technical depth in payment processing, scheme connectivity and the operation of highly available, regulated payments infrastructure. The role will define platform strategy, engineering standards, tooling and ways of working, while embedding a shift-left quality mindset across delivery. Success means delivering highly resilient, highly available, secure, scalable and compliant platforms that enable frequent, reliable change in a regulated banking environment. Key Responsibilities Own the strategy, design, build and run of real-time payments and cards platforms across the UK, Europe, the US and future international markets, including direct scheme connectivity and integrations with third-party payment infrastructure providers. Lead the delivery and operation of digital wallet capabilities, including Apple Pay and Google Pay implementations. Set the technical direction for payments and cards platforms, ensuring architectural choices support resilience, availability, scalability, performance, security and cost efficiency. Own the budget for the Payments and Cards engineering teams, ensuring effective investment in people, tooling and platforms. Build, lead and develop high-performing engineering teams, creating clear accountability, strong delivery discipline and a culture of engineering excellence. Ensure platforms are designed and operated to meet the following outcomes: Highly resilient — supporting local and cross-region disaster recovery requirements. Highly available — targeting 99.999% aggregate internal availability where appropriate. Highly scalable — supporting aggressive growth targets and future business volumes. Performant — meeting scheme performance requirements and exceeding client expectations on latency. Cost optimised — balancing client value, operational efficiency and ClearBank’s cost base. Establish scalable engineering quality standards, practices and governance across the payments and cards domain. Embed quality, observability, operational readiness and control requirements into delivery practices and CI/CD pipelines. Drive engineering productivity through AI-assisted and increasingly agentic software engineering, including the effective use of AI coding tools and multi-agent approaches across development, testing and engineering workflows, with appropriate risk, security and regulatory guardrails. Partner closely with the CTO, engineering leaders, product, risk, compliance and operations teams to ensure delivery decisions balance pace, quality and control. Ensure software development and platform operations meet regulatory, audit, resilience and compliance expectations. Skills & Experience Senior engineering leadership experience in payments, cards or highly regulated financial technology environments. Proven experience establishing, scaling and operating engineering teams, standards and practices. Direct experience integrating with, building against or operating connectivity to payment schemes or rails. Relevant examples include Faster Payments, Bacs or CHAPS in the UK; SEPA payment schemes and associated euro payment infrastructure in Europe; ACH or Fedwire in the US; or card networks and associated issuing or acquiring infrastructure. Alternatively, substantial experience delivering payment connectivity through a provider such as Form3 or an equivalent platform, with demonstrable technical depth in how payments are processed, routed and operated. Experience delivering or operating digital wallet capabilities, such as Apple Pay and Google Pay. Strong understanding of real-time, high-availability, high-throughput distributed systems. Strong background working in regulated environments, with practical experience of audit, compliance, operational resilience and control frameworks. Deep understanding of shift-left quality, test automation, modern quality engineering and secure software development practices. Experience using modern AI-enabled engineering tooling and a strong understanding of how agentic or multi-agent approaches can improve software development, testing and engineering delivery in a controlled and responsible way. Strong security mindset, with an appreciation of evolving threats, mitigations and secure platform design. Demonstrated ability to influence across multiple teams and senior stakeholders, including where direct line management is not present. Excellent collaboration and communication skills, with the ability to work effectively with engineering, product, risk, compliance and executive stakeholders. Sound judgement in balancing delivery pace, customer outcomes, regulatory expectations, operational risk and engineering quality. A little bit more about us! ClearBank is Where You Can belong: At ClearBank we think about Diversity, Equity and Inclusion (DE&I) a lot. Not because we think we should. But because we know we should – how else can we build a happy workforce and be successful as a business. We’re committed to making sure our teams reflect society. And we put energy and effort into making this a place where everyone feels at home, where they’re given the trust and encouragement to do their very best work. Here are some of the things we’re most proud of: 42% of our senior management roles are held by women Our enhanced family leave policies Launching our partnership with Code First Girls Increasing awareness of neurodiversity in the workplace through our partnership with the Inclusive Group Our hiring process and what you can expect: Application: a member of our talent acquisition team will review your application against the key requirements for the role and let you know within two weeks whether you’re moving forward to the next stage; Screening: You’ll spend 30-45 minutes speaking to one of our recruiters learning more about the role and ClearBank, and we’ll get it know more about you, your experience and how your skills align with the role (this will be via phone or Teams video call). You can expect to hear back from us within seven days following this meeting (if things are taking longer than expected, we’ll let you know that too); First Interview: You’ll spend one hour with a member of our hiring team focusing on your skills, competencies and your ways of working at the same time we’ll give you time to ask more questions about the role, the team and learn more about the ClearBank culture. This will be via Teams. Second Interview: This will be a competency-based interview with one or more members of our team. Final Stage: You will have a final meeting with the Head of Department. This will be around 45-60 minutes. Offer: Congratulations! Get ready to transform banking forever! Our commitment to you as a candidate: We will always try our best to get back to you within seven days of your interview whether you’ve been successful or not and provide you with feedback. Sometimes things take a little longer, so we may not have a decision to share but we will get it touch to let you know we need a little more time. We’re unable to provide specific individual feedback at the application or screening stage but know that your application was reviewed and considered carefully. We wish you the best of luck with your application and maybe we’ll be celebrating your new role at ClearBank soon! Equal Opportunities ClearBank is committed to ensuring equal opportunities throughout every stage of the recruitment process. description: Chief Medical Officer, UK/I & EMEA The Role Lyrebird is reshaping how clinical documentation happens across the NHS and in Ireland, and we’re looking for a Chief Medical Officer to be the senior clinical voice of the business. Reporting to the CEO, you’ll make sure everything we build, deploy and sell is clinically safe, evidence-based and genuinely useful to clinicians and patients. You’ll own our clinical safety and governance framework, including DCB0129 and oversight of the Clinical Safety Officer function. You’ll shape the product roadmap alongside Product and Engineering, build the evidence base that NHS and HSE buyers need, and act as a trusted peer to CCIOs, CMIOs, medical directors and ICB leaders. This role suits a practising or recently practising doctor who has led at a senior level in the NHS and knows digital health from the inside. You’re comfortable moving between a board presentation, a hazard log and a conversation with engineers in the same afternoon. You’ll enjoy the pace of a high-growth company, but you’ll never trade safety for speed. You believe clinical AI should be held to the same standards as the rest of medicine, and you want to be the person who proves it can be. About Us Lyrebird Health is transforming the quality and accessibility of healthcare by automating clinicians’ most time-consuming tasks. Thousands of clinicians across multiple disciplines use Lyrebird every day in environments where accuracy, safety, and time matter deeply. In the UK, that includes NHS trusts across Cheshire and Merseyside, Alder Hey Children’s, and the South West London Acute Provider Collaborative, one of the largest ambient AI deployments in the country. Everything we build is grounded in earning trust, reducing cognitive load, and delivering meaningful impact at scale. What you’ll do Lead Lyrebird’s clinical safety management system for the UK and Ireland, ensuring DCB0129 compliance, supporting customers with DCB0160, and providing senior oversight of our Clinical Safety Officers. Bring the clinical voice into the product roadmap, defining UK- and Ireland-specific workflows and leading clinical validation of new models, features and specialty templates before release. Own clinical incident management and chair our clinical governance and safety committee, reporting to the leadership team and board. Advise on the regulatory landscape, including MHRA medical device regulation, NHS England guidance on ambient voice technology, DTAC, and the EU AI Act for Ireland. Design and deliver a clinical evidence strategy, running evaluations and real-world studies with NHS and academic partners, publishing the results, and always reporting limitations honestly. Act as a trusted clinical peer to CCIOs, CMIOs, medical directors and digital leaders across NHS trusts, ICBs and the HSE, and represent Lyrebird at conferences, in the media and in national policy conversations. Bring clinical credibility to the commercial team by leading the clinical, safety and evidence sections of tenders, supporting pilots, and making sure every clinical claim we make stands up. Build and lead a UK and Ireland clinical team, and champion equity, patient safety and inclusive design across languages, accents and patient groups. What you’ll bring Full GMC registration with a licence to practise, in good standing. Significant senior clinical leadership experience in the NHS, such as Medical Director, Deputy or Associate Medical Director, or Clinical Director. Substantial digital health or clinical informatics leadership, for example as a CCIO, CMIO or senior clinical lead on an EPR or digital transformation programme. In-depth, practical knowledge of DCB0129 and DCB0160, clinical risk management, hazard logs and safety cases, plus a solid grasp of MHRA, DTAC, DSPT and NHS England AI guidance. A track record of designing, leading or publishing clinical evaluations, audits or research. Strong NHS networks and the ability to explain complex clinical, technical and regulatory issues clearly to boards, clinicians, engineers and patients. Nice to have Accredited Clinical Safety Officer training, and continuing clinical practice alongside the role. Experience in a health tech, MedTech or digital health company, ideally including evaluation of AI or NLP safety and performance. Knowledge of the EU AI Act, EU MDR and the Irish health system, or registration with the Medical Council of Ireland. Membership or fellowship of the Faculty of Clinical Informatics, or a national profile through the Royal Colleges, NHS England or a Health Innovation Network. Familiarity with clinical coding (SNOMED CT, ICD-10, OPCS-4), PRSB standards or the NICE Evidence Standards Framework. Every minute a clinician spends on documentation is a minute taken from their patients. In this role, you’ll help decide how ambient AI is safely adopted across the NHS and in Ireland, setting the standards that protect patients while giving clinicians time back to focus on care. We’re building a team that reflects the diversity of the people who benefit from our work. We want Lyrebird to be a place where everyone feels safe, supported, and able to thrive. A People Partner is planned to join later in 2027, and at that point the operational administration moves to them. This is also a role built with room to grow. Complex casework: Rather than simply handling harder cases, you’ll own the most complex cases end to end, with no hand back. People initiatives: Rather than contributing to initiatives someone else drives, you’ll own them from design through to embedding. Decision-making: Rather than escalating ambiguity upward, you’ll make the sensible call and document your reasoning. CPO partnership: Rather than acting in a support role to the CPO, you’ll be an operational partner they can confidently delegate to. To be clear about the level: The CPO still designs the People strategy and the systems architecture. You own how it runs day to day, and you’re trusted to run a whole initiative, not just a case. That is a different job to People Partner, not a bigger version of the same one. THE ROLE You’ll sit in the People team reporting to the Chief People Officer. Three strands make up the job: Casework: The employee relations situations with the most complexity or sensitivity land with you, start to finish. Initiatives: When the CPO needs a piece of work owned (a policy rollout, a wellbeing programme, a piece of the reward or benefits agenda), you take it from design through to something that runs. Operations: Until the People Partner joins, you’ll own payroll and benefits administration, onboarding, screening and security clearances, and keeping Rippling accurate. When the People Partner joins, they’ll report to the CPO. You won’t manage them formally, but you’ll lead their handover, you’ll be the person they come to first, and your judgement will set the standard for how this function operates day to day. WHERE THE ROLE STARTS AND STOPS New roles get vague, so here is the boundary as we see it today. Yours The most complex and sensitive employee relations casework, end to end. Full ownership of People initiatives, from design to embedding. Acting as the CPO’s operational partner on ambiguous or cross-cutting problems. Until the People Partner joins (planned for later in 2027): Payroll and benefits administration, including the monthly payroll cycle in Rippling and Mintago. Pre-onboarding, onboarding and probation. Background screening in Zinc. Security clearance coordination. Rippling data quality, workflows and reporting. Our working groups and committees. Once the People Partner joins: A structured handover of the operational core. Day-to-day guidance for the People Partner. Shared Ashby, which Talent Acquisition owns. You’ll work in it from offer through to start date on every hire until the People Partner joins, and on senior hires after that. Mentoring and supporting the People Partner on their casework and initiatives, once they join. Not yours Recruitment delivery, which sits with Talent Acquisition. The design of the People strategy, the operating model and the systems architecture, which sit with the CPO. Formal line management of the People Partner, who will report to the CPO. THE STACK Rippling: Our single source of truth. Until the People Partner joins you’ll run it day to day, including the monthly payroll cycle, data quality and workflows, and you’ll use its reporting at a level that supports whole initiatives. Zinc: Background screening. You’ll run checks for every new joiner until the People Partner joins, and stay close to the senior and sensitive hires after that. Ashby: Owned by Talent Acquisition. You’ll work in it from offer through to start date on the hires you’re responsible for. Claude: A daily tool here. You’ll use it for casework preparation, drafting policy and communications, and pulling together the analysis behind an initiative. Mintago: Our employee benefits and financial wellbeing platform (pensions, salary sacrifice and financial advice). You’ll administer it and keep enrolment accurate until the People Partner takes it on. WHAT YOU’LL DO Own the hardest casework. You’ll run our most complex and sensitive employee relations cases end to end, with the CPO there to sense-check rather than take over. Own initiatives, not tasks. You’ll take a People initiative from a rough brief to something that’s running and embedded, rather than handing it back once the interesting part is done. Run the operational core. Until the People Partner joins, you’ll own the monthly payroll cycle in Rippling, benefits administration including Mintago, onboarding, background screening and security clearances. Accurate, on time, and documented as you go. Hand it over well. When the People Partner arrives, you’ll give them a working system and a clear handover, then stay the person they come to first and the judgement others in the function measure themselves against. Partner with senior leaders. You’ll be credible with leaders on the most difficult conversations: complex change, capability, and situations without a clean playbook. Use AI properly. You’ll use Claude daily to take time out of your own week, checking anything that touches a decision about a person and owning the outcome. Improve what you find. You’ll spot the gaps in policy, process or practice before anyone else does, and bring the CPO a considered view on the fix, not just the problem. WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE AT 12 MONTHS You’re running the most complex ER cases with confidence, and the CPO isn’t being pulled into them. At least one or two People initiatives have gone from a rough brief to something genuinely embedded, owned by you. Payroll, benefits, onboarding and clearances run accurately and on time, and every process is documented well enough to hand over. You’ve helped shape the People Partner hire, so the handover is ready when they land. Senior leaders treat you as a credible operational partner, not an escalation point. You’ve made and documented sensible calls in genuinely ambiguous situations, and they’ve held up. The CPO can hand you an ambiguous problem and trust it gets shaped properly. WHO WE’RE LOOKING FOR Deep employee relations experience. You’ve run complex disciplinaries, grievances and change situations yourself, and you know exactly when to escalate and when not to. CIPD qualification, or solid progress towards it, is welcome. A track record of owning initiatives. You can point to work you took from a brief to something that actually ran, not just a project you contributed to. Hands-on with the operational detail. You’ve owned or closely supported a payroll cycle, benefits administration and onboarding, and you’re comfortable being accountable for their accuracy while also carrying the senior work. Credible with senior leaders. You can hold your own in a difficult conversation with someone under real pressure and be listened to. Comfortable operating near-autonomously. You don’t need a playbook for everything. You make a sensible call, write it down, and check it with the CPO afterwards. Ready to grow into people leadership. You won’t formally manage anyone at the start, but you’ll induct and guide the People Partner when they join, and you should want to lead a team as the structure catches up. Discreet and organised at volume. Complex casework and live initiatives, often at the same time. You’ll need a system, and it can’t be your memory. THE HONEST PART This role sits in an odd space for now: senior in scope and judgement, without a team underneath it yet. Until the People Partner joins later in 2027, you’ll also be the whole operational team, so a payroll deadline and a complex grievance can land in the same week. That eases as the function grows, but it means the authority you carry day to day has to come from the quality of your work, not a job title. You are not designing the People strategy or the systems architecture. The CPO does that. What you get instead is real ownership of the hardest cases and the initiatives that matter, a close working relationship with the CPO, and a genuine path toward leading the People Partner practice as it grows. This probably isn’t for you if you want a formal team from day one, or if you’d rather leave payroll and onboarding to someone else. It probably is for you if you want to prove you can run this function well enough, top to bottom, that a team gets built around you. If that sounds like the challenge you’ve been looking for, let’s talk. Proven success winning multi-million pound opportunities in defence, intelligence, or security markets. Deep domain knowledge of UK and European defence, procurement pathways, and decision-making cycles. Strong relationships and extant networks across MoD, NATO, and allied defence ecosystems. Technology fluency, ideally in AI, SaaS, or data analytics contexts. Exceptional communicator, able to brief ministers, generals, and CTOs with equal confidence. Desirable Experience in both government service and commercial technology companies. Familiarity with classified and open-source intelligence workflows. Understanding of European defence industrial and political landscapes. Entrepreneurial mindset with appetite for building new markets and capabilities. Comfortable in a high-growth, venture-backed environment. Experience building or scaling a BD function in a start-up or scale-up. Working proficiency in a second European language. title: General Counsel (Office based)
description: <p>We are hiring a <strong>General Counsel</strong> to lead Canonical’s global Legal and Compliance function and to build the legal architecture a public company needs — commercial contracting, corporate governance, intellectual property and compliance — in a software business that regularly does things the industry has not done before. You will report to the Chief Operating Officer and advise the CEO, CFO and the Board directly.</p> <p><strong>Location</strong>: <strong>Location</strong>: This role can be home-based in EMEA, or office-based in our London, UK office.</p> <h3><strong>About our team</strong></h3> <p>Canonical’s Legal and Compliance function is a distributed team across EMEA and the Americas. It owns the terms on which Ubuntu and our commercial products reach the market: open source and intellectual property licensing, enterprise and channel contracting, data protection, export controls and trade, competition, and the governance a company preparing to list has to be able to evidence.</p> <p>Canonical is founder-led, profitable and growing, and privately held with the intention to list on a public exchange. That makes this a function in transition. The work is as much building the architecture — a management layer across two regions, standard contracting positions, controls, policies and records — as it is advising on live matters, and it is done in a company that regularly does things the industry has not done before, so the precedents often do not exist.</p> <p>The team works with Product and Engineering on licensing and IP, with Security on customer assurance, with Finance on listing readiness and controls, and with Sales on the commitments we make to customers. As General Counsel you lead that team, set its standards, and advise the CEO, COO, CFO and the Board and its committees directly.</p> <h3><strong>What you'll do</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Lead the global Legal and Compliance function: set its structure, standards and priorities across EMEA and the Americas, so the business gets consistent answers wherever it operates.</li> <li>Build the management layer: hire and develop managers, set objectives, review performance against a clear bar, and address under-performance directly rather than waiting it out.</li> <li>Set the operating cadence of the function: how legal work is taken in and prioritised, what internal clients can expect and when, and how workload and risk are reported to the leadership team.</li> <li>Own public-market readiness on the legal side: corporate governance, group and entity structure, delegated authority, policies, disclosure controls and records, in partnership with Finance.</li> <li>Advise the CEO, COO, CFO and the Board, and support Board and committee meetings.</li> <li>Own the commercial contracting framework: standard templates, negotiating positions, and a deviation and escalation process that makes commitments visible before they are signed.</li> <li>Lead intellectual property and open source licensing strategy: permissive and copyleft licences, trademark, and the terms on which Ubuntu and our products are distributed.</li> <li>Own the global compliance programme: data protection and privacy, export controls and trade compliance, anti-bribery and corruption, competition, and AI regulation.</li> <li>Manage litigation, disputes and regulatory engagement, and own the external counsel panel, its budget and the quality of its work.</li> <li>Advise on M&A, partnerships, strategic alliances and financing as the company grows.</li> </ul> <h3><strong>What we are looking for in you</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Qualified as a lawyer, with a law degree or equivalent and an active licence to practise in an EMEA or Americas jurisdiction.</li> <li>In-house legal leadership in a software or technology company — a business that licenses its own products, rather than one that buys technology to run its operations.</li> <li>Commercial technology contracting: enterprise software and subscription agreements, channel and reseller agreements, cloud and services, and hardware manufacturer agreements.</li> <li>Open source licensing: permissive and copyleft licences, trademark, and how open source communities work in practice.</li> <li>Corporate governance for a listed company, or for one preparing to list: board and committee support, delegated authority, disclosure and controls.</li> <li>Depth in at least two of: data protection and privacy, IP and trademark, export controls and trade, competition, or disputes.</li> <li>Leading a distributed legal team, including managing managers across regions and time zones.</li> <li>Building or restructuring an in-house legal function, including deciding what is retained, delegated and sent to external counsel.</li> <li>A track record of setting and holding a high performance bar: hiring well, developing people, and dealing with under-performance directly rather than waiting it out.</li> <li>An exceptional academic track record from both high school and university.</li> <li>Professional written and spoken English, with excellent drafting and presentation skills.</li> <li>Ability to travel internationally two to four times a year, for company events up to two weeks long.</li> </ul> <h3><strong>Nice-to-have skills</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Experience taking a company through an IPO, or practising as counsel inside a listed company.</li> <li>A technical or engineering background, or fluency in how software is built and shipped.</li> <li>Experience of a subscription or recurring-revenue business model.</li> <li>A qualification in more than one jurisdiction.</li> </ul> <p><strong>How we work</strong></p> <p>We look for a track record of going above-and-beyond expectations to achieve outstanding results, backed by self-motivation and drive. Our people deliver their work precisely, taking care to deliver correctness and clarity. Reliability is at our core, where colleagues deliver high quality work that builds trust and confidence. We make ourselves accessible, collaborating to build products and systems that are usable. Finally we are adroit, blending enthusiasm, knowledge, adaptability, style and character.</p> <h3><strong>What we offer colleagues</strong></h3> <p>We consider geographical location, experience, and performance in shaping compensation worldwide. We revisit compensation annually (and more often for graduates and associates) to ensure we recognize outstanding performance. In addition to base pay, we offer a performance-driven annual bonus or commission. We provide all team members with additional benefits which reflect our values and ideals. We balance our programs to meet local needs and ensure fairness globally.</p> <ul> <li>Distributed work environment with twice-yearly team sprints in person.</li> <li>Personal learning and development budget of USD 2,000 per year.</li> <li>Bi-annual compensation review.</li> <li>Company recognition rewards.</li> <li>40 days annual leave per annum, including public holidays and our All Company holiday periods.</li> <li>Maternity and paternity leave.</li> <li>Team Member Assistance Program & Wellness Platform.</li> <li>Opportunity to travel to new locations to meet colleagues, with Priority Pass for lounge access.</li> </ul> <h3><strong>About Canonical</strong></h3> <p>Canonical is a pioneering tech firm at the forefront of the global move to open source. Our platform, Ubuntu, is very widely used in breakthrough enterprise initiatives such as public cloud, data science, AI, engineering innovation, and IoT. Our customers include the world's leading public cloud and silicon providers, and industry leaders in many sectors. title: People Performance Manager
description: 📈 Who We Are: We are rebuilding the energy transaction, making it transparent and fair. We're rebuilding how energy is bought and sold. That means cutting out middlemen, connecting businesses directly with renewable generators, and ensuring every transaction is traceable and transparent . We're a 160+ person team - operators, data scientists, engineers, customer champions and energy experts - backed by top-tier investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, Hitachi Ventures, Allianz, AlbionVC and Atomico. We closed a $75M Series B round in early 2026, taking our total funding to $94M, and we now power energy for over 4,000 UK businesses across 8,500+ sites , with over £75m in value returned to businesses and generators so far. We're a technology company solving the energy industry, not an energy company. Some people call us a neo-utility, the neo-bank idea, applied to energy. The industry is noticing. We were crowned Europe's Most Exciting Tech Company at the GP Bullhound Allstars awards , came in at #6 on LinkedIn's Top Startups 2026 in the UK, #7 on the Scaling Europe 50 of Europe's fastest-growing companies, and #14 on Sifted's AI 100 . Learn more about us on our website . 🚀 The Role We're hiring a People Performance Manager to join our Performance Service. tem is growing fast. Our goal is to get better as we get bigger - revenue growing faster than headcount. In practice that means keeping our strongest people engaged and performing, getting new joiners productive quickly, and enabling our leaders to multiply their impact over time. Most companies solve that with layers of management. We don't. Our leaders (Player-Coaches) coach their teams while staying hands-on with the work, which means the systems around them have to do more of the lifting. That's where the Performance Service comes in. We're a team of four, and we own how tem runs as an organisation: the operating rhythm (how work gets planned, tracked, escalated and reported), the onboarding and development that build capability, the frameworks that define what good performance looks like and how people progress and get paid, and the operational backbone of contracts, benefits and payroll. We don't own recruitment. We're adding a second Performance Partner because we need more hands on deck - both partnering with our leaders day to day, and building the frameworks that support them. Your patch is sustained performance - the part that runs continuously once someone is through the door. You'll carry a portfolio of leaders across our Engines and Services that you're accountable for, and you'll co-own the frameworks that sit underneath them alongside the rest of the team. You will not be handed a finished playbook to administer. You'll report into the Performance Service Manager. HR experience is welcome but not required - we're open to operators, people who've led teams, and the sort of person who ends up owning whatever the company needs next. In your first 12 months, you might: Become the first call for a portfolio of leaders on anything to do with their people - performance calls, team decisions and hard conversations. Co-design how progression, performance standards, evaluation and reward actually work at tem, alongside the rest of the Performance team. Handle live cases end to end - performance management, difficult conversations, exits and restructures. Use AI and automation so the operational layer runs itself and your time goes on judgement, not process. Turn recurring employee and manager pain points into better processes, tools, guidance or self-service, and measure whether they work. 🛠️ Responsibilities Coach and challenge: be a leader's first call on anything to do with their people - a decision they want a second view on, coaching on how to handle a situation, or a read on employment law - and hold a position when you disagree with them. Raise the bar: hold leaders to a high standard on performance, potential, pay and progression - help them make sharper calls, and hold consistency across your patch. Handle live cases end to end: performance management, difficult conversations, exits and restructures. Build to delight: shape how progression, performance standards, evaluation and reward actually work at tem, alongside the rest of the Performance team. We treat our people like top athletes, and our aim is to delight them at every step of their employee experience - the systems around them have to express that at every contact point. Design for our shape, not the textbook: we index on outcomes and impact in everything - how progression works, how teams are structured, what leaders spend their time on. Most standard people frameworks assume a management hierarchy we don't have. Automate the repeatable: use AI and automation so the operational layer runs itself and your time goes on judgement, not process. Think in process, scalability and iteration: turn recurring employee and manager pain points into better processes, tools, guidance or self-service. Measure whether they work and redesign when they don't fit the purpose. ✅ Requirements You do not need a CIPD qualification, and you do not need to have worked in a large, established HR function. You might have been a founder's associate or Chief of Staff at a Series A or B startup, holding the place together while it scaled. You might have built a People function from scratch and taken it from a one-person band to a well-oiled machine. You might have run a team or an Operations function where the people calls were effectively yours, even if People or HR never appeared in your job title. Or you might have done a different job that helped you build the skills below. A background in HR might help you do this job well, but it is not a requirement. Must-Haves You've held real accountability for decisions on people - you've partnered with leaders, or managed a team yourself, where hiring, performance and exit calls were either yours or made on your guidance. You can be trusted with the hardest conversations in the business and you're recognised for how you handle them, and you understand how decisions about people shape culture and employer brand - balancing efficiency with empathy. You've worked in or towards building a high-performance culture, and you're a confident challenger who carries conviction and can influence leadership decisions. You're comfortable operating without a playbook, in a company where the requirements and the shape of your role change constantly. You think from first principles, get to the root cause of complex problems, weigh competing considerations and anticipate second-order consequences. You're fluent with Notion, automation and AI tooling - your instinct is to build the thing rather than do it manually a second time - and you write clearly enough that a busy person reads it once and comes away with a clear idea of the situation and the next actions. Desirable Employment relations experience in the UK, Europe or the US - we operate across the UK and Europe today, with plans to expand to the US soon. Experience working across multiple countries, including employer of record arrangements. Compensation and benchmarking experience - salary banding, pay review cycles, market data. 🎁 Benefits & Perks Stock options so everyone has ownership in our mission. 25 days holiday plus public holidays. Swap public holidays for the ones that matter most to you, and enjoy your birthday off. Remote first and flexible working, with clear core hours and no internal meetings on Friday afternoons. Up to GBP1,200 or EUR1,400 per year for your remote setup. Up to GBP150 or EUR170 per month for wellbeing. 🤝 Interview Process We move fast. Most processes take 2 to 3 weeks from first chat to offer. If you need us to adapt anything, let us know. Intro call with our Talent team. Skills interview, which might include a practical exercise we may ask you to prepare in advance. Hiring Manager interview. Bar Raiser interview with leadership stakeholders. We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, experiences, and identities, including those that are traditionally underrepresented in the tech and energy sectors. If you’re excited about this role but not sure you meet every requirement, we’d still love to hear from you. Your unique perspective could be exactly what we’re looking for. description: Relay is fundamentally reshaping how goods move in an online era. We're assembling the most talent-dense team the logistics industry has ever seen Relay’s Mission is to free commerce from friction . Today, high delivery costs act as a hidden tax on e-commerce, quietly shaping what can be sold online and limiting who can participate. We envision a world where more goods move more freely between more people , making the online shopping experience seamless and accessible to everyone. THE TEAM • ~160 people , around half in engineering, product and data • 45+ advanced degrees across computer science, mathematics and operations research • Thousands of data points captured, calculated, analysed and predicted for every single parcel we handle • An intellectually vibrant culture of first‑principles thinking , tight feedback loops and relentless experimentation The role Every parcel through our sort centres is handled by an operative. As Operations Manager, Operative Acquisition you'll own operative supply across our sortation sites: enough suitable, trained, compliant and active operatives to fill every shift. You'll build the funnel, reporting and automation that make supply repeatable rather than manual, and keep it ahead of demand as volume rises. Volumes rise sharply into November and December. Supply, not demand, will be the constraint. This role exists to make sure it isn't. You'll be the single owner of the operative funnel, working across acquisition (including paid channels), Live Operations, our site teams, and Product and Engineering, who build the integrations the funnel runs on. You'll write SQL, ship automation, and spend time at our sort centres seeing how new starters actually land. A growth or operations background. You treat supply as a daily number and act the same day it slips Confident in SQL (BigQuery or similar). You build dashboards from raw data, not static trackers Experience running a high-volume hiring or onboarding funnel, ideally for a frontline workforce A working understanding of Right to Work checks, enough to see how checks and re-checks affect the funnel and operative status. Desirable Comfortable with paid acquisition, Google Ads or similar, enough to read performance and brief changes when a site runs short Experience onboarding couriers or drivers at a carrier or delivery platform Experience working with Product and Engineering on integrations or APIs Experience with predictive or candidate-quality modelling Strong forecasting skills and an understanding of seasonality Compensation, Benefits & Workplace Generous equity, richer than 99% of European startups, with annual top-ups to share Relay's success Private health & dental coverage, so comprehensive you'd need to be a partner at a Magic Circle law firm to match it 25 days of holidays Enhanced parental leave Hardware of your choice Extensive perks (gym subsidies, cycle-to-work, Friday office lunch, covered Uber home and dinner for late nights, and more) Located in Shoreditch, our office set-up enables the kind of in-person interactions that drive impact. You take ownership from start to finish and do what it takes to deliver when it counts. People-Powered Greatness : You invest in your teammates. You give and receive feedback with care and candour. You build trust through high standards and shared success. Grow the Whole Pie : You seek out win-win solutions for merchants, couriers, and our customers, because when they thrive, so do we. title: Senior Campaign Manager (Temp Contract)
description: About Pleo Messy spend management is tricky business. And tedious processes are a lose-lose situation for all involved, not just finance. At Pleo, we're changing that. We build spend solutions that make managing money seamless, empowering, and surprisingly effective for finance teams and employees alike - with a vision to help all businesses ‘go beyond’. The word ‘Pleo’ actually means ‘more than you’d expect’, and living by that mantra has been the secret to our success over the last 10 years. Now, we’re at a pivotal moment in our journey; every move we make has a direct impact on our 40,000+ customers, our business, and our collective success. We need people who take pride in uncovering customer needs, who turn complex problems into simple solutions, challenge the way things are done (respectfully), and always aim high. With great ambitions driving us forward, we can’t say we’ve got this whole thing figured out. And frankly, that’s half the fun! What we can say is that we’re a driven, progressive, and, importantly, a kind bunch of 850+ people from over 100 nationalities, all committed to delivering the future of business spending, together. About the role We're looking for a Senior Integrated Campaign Manager, Brand & GTM to join our Integrated Marketing team at Pleo. In this role, you'll help architect, roll out, project manage, and drive the Go-To-Market (GTM) execution for our major 2027 brand marketing strategy and campaigns and be part of turning brand strategy, positioning, and creative concepts into operational GTM blueprints as we scale our multi-segment (SMB, Mid-Market, Enterprise) reach across 6 key European markets. If you're excited about high-visibility, full-funnel orchestration and balancing long-term brand equity building with full-funnel conversion, and are passionate about integrated brand and GTM marketing in high-growth B2B SaaS, then this is the opportunity for you! Please bear in mind this role is a temporary contract of 1 year. Who you’ll be working with and reporting to You’ll report to our Director of Integrated Marketing and work closely with teams in Brand Marketing, Digital, Field/Events, Content, PR, Product Marketing (PMM), Marketing Ops, Data, and Sales/Growth channels. Our team is highly collaborative and dedicated to bridging top-of-funnel brand awareness with lower-funnel acquisition, ensuring every campaign moment translates into market salience, customer engagement, and measurable business impact. You’ll also have the chance to partner with teams across country teams, local market stakeholders, Sales Leadership, SDRs, and Field squads to ensure success. What you’ll be doing As a Senior Campaign Manager, you will: Integrated GTM Architecture & Strategic Planning : Translate the overarching 2027 brand strategy into actionable, full-funnel GTM campaign blueprints across SMB, Mid-Market, and Enterprise segments, architecting campaign flighting and distribution models across 6 European markets. The "Master Brief" & Cross-Functional Squad Leadership : Own and author comprehensive Integrated Campaign Master Briefs, leading the operational rhythm of cross-functional squads to execute multi-channel strategies (OOH, Paid Social, VIP activations, Digital, ABM) on time and within scope. Localization & Regional Adaptation : Partner with country teams and local market stakeholders to ensure master campaign frameworks balance global consistency with local relevance and execution precision. Strategic Brand Partnership & Enablement : Serve as the strategic execution peer to the Brand Marketing Lead, while partnering with Sales Leadership, SDRs, and Field teams to equip customer-facing squads with the stories, tools, and campaign momentum needed to capitalize on campaign-generated intent. Campaign Operations, Budget & ROI Accountability : Maintain and protect the integrated campaign master calendar, manage and allocate the multi-country integrated campaign budget, and partner with Marketing Ops, Data, and Brand Intelligence to track brand lift, consideration, pipeline growth, and closed-won impact. What you bring You’ll thrive in this role if you have: A proven track record leading multi-million dollar, multi-country, full-funnel integrated campaigns in high-growth B2B SaaS or tech environments. Deep experience taking high-level brand frameworks and translating them into multi-channel GTM blueprints across varied audience segments (SMB to Enterprise). High proficiency in aligning cross-functional teams (Creative, Digital, PR, Ops, Sales) and holding squads accountable to tight deadlines and complex campaign launches. Deep understanding of how to run campaigns across diverse European markets, with a clear perspective on modular campaign design and local adaptation. Experience with tracking brand-to-pipeline performance metrics, campaign flighting dynamics, brand lift, consideration, and total ROI. A background in integrated marketing, GTM campaign management, or brand marketing orchestration within B2B technology or SaaS. Why is this role a good fit for you This role is a good fit for you if: You thrive as the operational bridge between high-level brand strategy and lower-funnel demand generation, turning concepts into structured GTM blueprints. You love leading cross-functional squads across multiple international markets, balancing consistency with local nuances across 6 key European countries. You take pride in end-to-end accountability, from authoring master briefs and handling multi-country budgets to tracking downstream pipeline velocity and closed-won revenue impact. This role is not a good fit for you if: You prefer focusing purely on high-level creative ideation, copy, or audience insight development without building the operational execution machinery. You prefer running single-channel or single-market marketing initiatives rather than orchestrating complex, multi-segment (SMB to Enterprise), multi-channel matrices. You are uncomfortable navigating data, campaign flighting performance, budget allocations, and downstream pipeline attribution alongside brand metrics. How you’ll develop in this role In your first 6 months at Pleo, you’ll: Lead the architecture and rollout of the 2027 integrated brand campaign calendar across all target European markets. Collaborate with the Brand Marketing Lead, country teams, and Marketing Ops to stand up the Master Briefing framework and streamline cross-functional execution rhythms. Grow your skills in full-funnel orchestration and multi-market scale, driving measurable brand lift, consideration, and downstream pipeline velocity as Pleo continues to expand. The location Please note: We can hire on a hybrid or in-person set-up in any of the locations listed on the advert but you will need to be physically based in the country of your choice with a valid right to work . We are unable to offer visa sponsorship for this role in any of the listed locations. Show me the benefits! Your own Pleo card (no more out-of-pocket spending!) Lunch is on us for your work days - enjoy catered meals or receive a lunch allowance based on your local office Comprehensive private healthcare - depending on your location, coverage options include Vitality, Alan or Médis 25 days of annual leave + public holidays (additional days may apply in select countries based on local standards). For our Team, we offer both hybrid and fully remote working options We use MyndUp to give our employees access to free mental health and well-being support with great success so far Paid parental leave - we want to make sure that we're supportive of families and help you feel that you don't have to compromise your family due to work The interview process We want to ensure you are set-up for success and understand what will be expected of you. If your application is successful, our interview process is as follows: Intro call: A 30-minute chat with our Talent Partner to discuss the role and your background. Hiring Manager Interview: A 45 minute chat to deep dive into your experience Challenge & Team Interview: We will send you a take home test and invite you to present during a 60 minute team interview. This is an opportunity to show us how you would handle the day to day of the role Final Interview : A final interview with a senior leader Transparency is important to us so we also wanted to share some insights about what we’re looking for in applications to ensure you can set yourself up for success! Last time we hired for this role, we received a total vast number of applications but only a few were selected for an intro call.Some of the key reasons why previous candidates didn’t make it past the application screening stage include: CV writing and content: we receive a lot of CVs, and many of them are AI-generated. We love seeing people leverage AI—it’s a big focus for us internally too—but without human intervention, these CVs can sometimes become generic and fail to show a candidate in the best light. What we're really looking for is the specific details of real impact that only you know from your previous experience. A top tip from us is to use the “Achieved X, as measured by Y, by doing Z” formula (credit: Laszlo Bock, ~2014) to give a really clear picture of what you’ve worked on. A final note: including links to your previous companies' websites is a huge help and allows us to truly understand your background! Application care: every single application we receive is reviewed by a human (yes, hundreds of them) because we believe that candidates' efforts should be matched by an equal level of human care. This means that we expect a similar level of attention put into your application. Read and answer the application questions carefully, they make a huge difference in our decision-making process. Profile to role fit: highlight most important aspects of the role, points that might get misunderstood, any specific industry requirements etc. About your application English first. Since it's our company language, please submit your application in English. You’ll be using it a lot if you join us. A fair look for everyone. Our talent team reads every single application to ensure the process is fair. To keep things running smoothly, we only accept applications through our system—our support team can’t pass on calls or emails. Diversity drives us. We can only reach our goals if our team reflects the world around us. That starts with you hitting apply, even if you don't tick every single box. We encourage people from all backgrounds and experiences to join us. Interview at your best. We want you to feel comfortable throughout the process. If you have any accessibility requirements or need a specific format, email ----- We’ll design a process that works for you. Your data is safe.
